Fetch the share of students with IEPs, district rows by grade band or school rows

Source: R/fetch_sped_share.R
fetch_sped_share.Rd

Rows of the share of students with an IEP, at the finest grain New Jersey publishes, in the shape sped_all_vs_all and sped_like_for_like read. Every value is from a NJDOE file.

Usage

fetch_sped_share(
  end_year,
  basis = c("lea_idea", "school_report", "school_spr")
)

Arguments

end_year

ending school year. "lea_idea": 2023-2026. "school_report": 2021-2025.

basis

"lea_idea" (default) or "school_report". Also accepts "school_spr": school-only rates for 2023-2025 from the complete bundled 2024-25 EnrollmentTrendsByStudentGroup sheet. That basis keeps source_value and school_year, leaves n_sped NA, reads enrollment and grade spans from EnrollmentTrendsbyGrade, and preserves rounded or bounded rates in pct_sped_lo/hi. No count is recovered from a rounded share. The SPR guide defines this as students classified for special education divided by total enrollment. Enrollment is attributed to the school reporting enrollment; this differs from accountability's sending-school attribution for specialized receiving schools. School years 2023 and 2024 are historical rows in the 2025 release.

Value

A data frame with end_year, entity_level (state, district or school), district_id, school_id, district_name, school_name, grade_band (all, elementary, middle, high), grade_low, grade_high, n_sped, n_enrolled, pct_sped, pct_sped_lo, pct_sped_hi, is_charter, construct, count_date and source_file. Suppressed values are NA, never zero.

Details

Each basis uses its own construct and grain:

"lea_idea" (default, 2023-2026)

District (LEA) rows. For 2023-2025, an all row per district and the state from the IDEA classification files (count, enrollment, rate). For every year, rows for elementary (K-5), middle (6-8) and high (9-12) from NJDOE's response to OPRA request C255254 (see fetch_sped_by_grade), over the same year's Fall Enrollment by grade. Pre-K is left out of every band. A band with a suppressed grade cell (a count under 5) has n_sped = NA and pct_sped_lo/hi from the published bound of 1 to 4 for each suppressed cell. A cell NJDOE left blank is zero students: wherever nothing is suppressed, the OPRA grade cells sum to the IDEA child count for every district in 2023-2025. The band rows carry no pct_sped: NJDOE publishes counts by grade, and the helpers pool the counts. 2025-26 is flagged: known OPRA counts fall 8 percent from 2024-25, there is no IDEA file yet, and the call warns.

"school_report" (2021-2025, live)

School rows, plus district and state rows, from the School Performance Reports: Students with Disabilities as a percent of enrollment, one decimal, with no suppression. n_enrolled is the same report's total enrollment, and grade_low/grade_high are the lowest and highest grades with students in that report. This is a different construct from the IDEA child count (in 2024-25 the statewide figure is 18.1 percent against 17.35 percent for IDEA, and some schools differ by more); NJDOE does not explain the gap. Downloads the School Performance Reports workbooks, which are large.

"school_spr" (2023-2025, bundled)

School-only rates from the 2024-25 release's enrollment trends, preserving historical school-year labels, source text and rounding bounds. n_sped remains NA. The same report supplies enrollment and grade spans.

is_charter is TRUE for the state's charter sector (county code 80) and for the three Camden renaissance operators in county 07 (1799, 1801, 1802) listed by the NJDOE Renaissance School Project, and FALSE otherwise.

See also

fetch_sped, fetch_sped_by_grade

Examples

# 1. District rows by grade band, with the IDEA all-grades row
share <- fetch_sped_share(2025)

#> Unknown column name: Column2

# 2. Band counts for the district-run and charter sectors
library(dplyr)
share %>%
  filter(entity_level == "district", grade_band != "all") %>%
  group_by(is_charter, grade_band) %>%
  summarise(n_sped = sum(n_sped, na.rm = TRUE), n_enrolled = sum(n_enrolled, na.rm = TRUE))
